tax.text: Lee authored AB 259, a tax on extreme wealth, arguing it would raise billions for schools and services while affecting almost no one.
tax.quote: 99.9% of people would not be impacted by the Wealth Tax, yet it could generate over $20 billion in revenue for our schools, roads, and essential services.

housing.text: Lee's platform calls for smart-growth policies to build more mixed-use, mixed-income housing in dense areas, plus public 'social housing.'
housing.quote: Promote smart growth policies that will create more mixed-use housing in dense areas that are available to mixed-income levels

immigration.text: Lee authored a resolution affirming the Legislature's commitment to birthright citizenship.
immigration.quote: Affirming the Legislature's commitment to birthright citizenship (AJR 5 of 2025)

health.text: Lee champions universal, single-payer health care and authored AB 1900 toward that goal.
health.quote: Universal health care for everyone (AB 1900 of 2025)

energy.text: Lee's platform calls for ending fracking and California's reliance on fossil fuels.
energy.quote: Ending fracking and our reliance on fossil fuels

tax.text: Hsia says he wants to protect Proposition 13 and opposes the property-tax reassessment provision of Proposition 19.
tax.quote: He also wants to protect Proposition 13 and oppose the property tax reassessment clause in Proposition 19

housing.text: Hsia argues overregulation drives up housing costs and wants to streamline fees and bureaucratic delays to lower construction costs.
housing.quote: Overregulation, he argues, is one of the single biggest drivers of unaffordable housing in California

safety.text: Hsia supports funding Proposition 36 and proposes license plate readers and cameras at high-crime intersections.
safety.quote: He fully supports funding Proposition 36, which allows prosecutors to charge repeat drug and theft offenders with felonies.
